# onyx_integration (Resource)

An integration: an MCP server or an HTTP API from an OpenAPI document, managed on the Onyx integrations API (`/admin/integrations`). Set exactly one of `server_url` and `openapi_document`. This resource replaces `onyx_mcp_server` and `onyx_custom_tool`. Needs Onyx v5.1 or later. Import with the numeric integration id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "weather_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# An MCP server with one API key for the organization.
resource "onyx_integration" "weather" {
  name                                = "Weather"
  description                         = "Forecasts and alerts."
  server_url                          = "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
  auth_mode                           = "shared"
  auth_method                         = "api_key"
  header_template                     = { Authorization = "Bearer {api_key}" }
  organization_credentials_wo         = { api_key = var.weather_api_key }
  organization_credentials_wo_version = 1
}

# An HTTP API from an OpenAPI document. Each user signs in with their own key.
resource "onyx_integration" "tickets" {
  name             = "Tickets"
  openapi_document = file("${path.module}/tickets.openapi.yaml")
  auth_mode        = "individual"
  auth_method      = "api_key"
  header_template  = { "X-Api-Key" = "{api_key}" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auth_mode` (String) Who signs in: `none`, `shared` (one connection for the organization) or `individual` (each user connects).
- `name` (String) Name that users see.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_method` (String) How to sign in: `api_key`, `oauth2` or `onyx_login`. Required unless `auth_mode` is `none`.
- `description` (String) Description that users and the model see.
- `enabled` (Boolean) When `false`, no user can use the integration. Onyx sets `true` on create.
- `header_template` (Map of String) HTTP headers sent on each call. Values can use `{placeholder}` fields, for example `{ Authorization = "Bearer {api_key}" }`. The connection supplies the field values.
- `installation_policy` (String) Company install setting: `REQUIRED`, `DEFAULT`, `AVAILABLE` (the default) or `NOT_AVAILABLE`. With `NOT_AVAILABLE`, the integration is private: only the API key's user and the integration's shares can use it.
- `openapi_document` (String) OpenAPI document of the HTTP API, as JSON or YAML text, for example `file("openapi.yaml")`. Each operation becomes an action. Onyx does not return the document as sent, so the provider keeps the configured text and a refresh does not detect changes made outside Terraform. An import reads the document Onyx stored, so the first apply after an import can update the integration in place.
- `organization_credentials_wo` (Map of String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Values of the `header_template` fields for the organization connection, for example `{ api_key = var.api_key }`. Use with `auth_mode = "shared"`. Terraform sends them on create and stores nothing. Raise `organization_credentials_wo_version` to send new values. Needs Terraform 1.11 or later.
- `organization_credentials_wo_version` (Number) Rotation counter for `organization_credentials_wo`. Terraform never stores a write-only value and so cannot tell that the secret changed; raise this number to make the next apply send the current one. Do not derive it from the secret itself — unlike the secret, this number is kept in state.
- `server_url` (String) URL of the MCP server. Conflicts with `openapi_document`. When Onyx can sign in at once (`auth_mode = "none"`), it calls the server on create and update to load its actions, so the server must answer.
- `transport` (String) MCP transport: `STREAMABLE_HTTP` (the default) or `SSE`. Only with `server_url`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric integration id.
- `kind` (String) `mcp` for an MCP server or `api` for an HTTP API.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
# Import by numeric integration id.
terraform import onyx_integration.weather 12
```
